landing.tagline: A Pluggable Multi-Agent AI Framework in Go
landing.subtitle: Every component is an interface — Model, Memory, Tools, Guards, Approver, Hooks, Observer — assembled by a 7-stage runtime. Three multi-agent modes (sub-agent delegation, transfer-to team, DAG orchestrate), ACP v1, layered governance, WASM plugins, and IM channels (Feishu / WeChat / WeCom). Agent is pure config; the runtime is the execution body.
landing.mentalModel: Agent is pure configuration. kernel.Runtime is a 7-stage mainline loop wiring independent top-level packages via DI. Multi-agent comes in three shapes: SubAgent (sync as-tool delegation), Team (transfer_to_* control handoff), Orchestrate (LLM-planned DAG, parallel execution). IM channels are process-level daemons — the agent runs the same; the channel is just another transport.

lines.text: ACP v1 server ready on stdio (VSCode/Zed)
→ I'm hwcloud, a pluggable multi-agent framework...
QR code → scan to provision bot

pluggable.title: Pluggable interfaces
pluggable.desc: Model, Memory, Tools, Guards, Approver, Hooks, Observer — every component is an interface injected via Deps. Agent holds only config; the runtime wires the rest.

multiagent.title: Three multi-agent modes
multiagent.desc: SubAgent (sync as-tool delegation), Team (transfer_to_* control handoff with loop detection), Orchestrate (LLM-planned DAG, parallel batches, auto-replan). Composable — an agent can be in a Team and a Plan step.

acp.title: ACP v1 + IM channels
acp.desc: ACP v1 over stdio (VSCode/Zed/opencode). Plus three IM transports: Feishu (WebSocket cards, streaming, approval buttons), WeChat (ilinkai long-poll, one-shot replies), WeCom (native streaming). Process-level daemons.

runtime.title: 7-stage runtime
runtime.desc: guard.in → memory.fetch → prompt.build → model.call → guard.out → tool.execute → memory.append. Each stage emits observe events; policy + execution live inside tool.execute.

governance.title: Layered governance
governance.desc: rules → safety → approval memory → human. First-match rules, read-only auto-allow, multi-key ALL-must-match memory, fail-closed human layer. Plan mode removes execution tools for safe exploration.

plugins.title: WASM plugins + sandbox
plugins.desc: 6 plugin types + cron-scheduled jobs, 28 host exports, wazero runtime, Rust PDK. OS-native sandbox (Linux bwrap / macOS Seatbelt) confines shell, file, and network.

landing.archTeaserDesc: Agent is pure config; kernel.Runtime is a thin orchestrator running a 7-stage loop. The real subsystems — context, execution, governance, session, provider, eventbus — are independent top-level packages injected as interfaces, not kernel subdirectories.

out.title: Transports
out.note: ACP v1 / REST+SSE / Feishu / WeChat / WeCom

firstRun: Build the CLI: go build -o hwcloud ./cmd/cli/
Optionally place AGENTS.md (working rules) and SOUL.md (persona) in ~/.hwcloud/profile/.
Run ./hwcloud serve --acp for an ACP client (VSCode/Zed), or --port 8080 for REST + SSE.
Toggle capabilities: --guard on, --approver on, --sandbox for OS-level confinement.
Drop .wasm files in ~/.hwcloud/plugins/ — they auto-load by type.

iacCard.title: IAC MCP Server
iacCard.desc: Deploy cloud infrastructure from AI chat via MCP — plan, provision, estimate cost, apply, and destroy, all in natural language.

landing.tuiDesc: Prefer a terminal UI over raw CLI? hwcloud also ships a Rust ratatui TUI client (ACP over stdio) — build it and point it at any ACP backend.

arch.title: Architecture
arch.intro: Agent is pure configuration; kernel.Runtime is a thin orchestrator running a 7-stage mainline loop. The real subsystems are independent top-level packages wired through Deps — not kernel internals.

layers.title: Agent is pure config
layers.desc: agent.Agent holds only fields: SystemPrompts, Model, Prompt, InGuard, OutGuard, MaxTurns, MaxWorkingTokens, MaxCompressedTokens, SubAgents. No execution methods. New(*agent.Agent, Deps) separates config from runtime.

layers.title: 7-stage mainline loop
layers.desc: observer.go declares 7 stage constants. run() emits observe events in this order; policy + execution are merged inside executeTools (no separate stage). memory.append fires after every committed message.
layers.example:
// observer.go
StageGuardIn  = "guard.in"
StageMemoryFetch = "memory.fetch"
StagePromptBuild = "prompt.build"
StageModelCall   = "model.call"
StageGuardOut    = "guard.out"
StageToolExecute = "tool.execute"
StageMemoryAppend = "memory.append"

layers.title: Deps-injected top-level packages
layers.desc: context, execution, governance, session, provider, eventbus are independent packages, not kernel subdirectories. Runtime holds them as interface fields via Deps. kernel is a thin orchestrator, not an implementation.

layers.title: Governance policy chain
layers.desc: Engine.Evaluate is one inline method: rules (first-match glob) → safety (read-only tools auto-allow) → memory (multi-key ALL must match) → human (fail-closed). Shell commands decompose into atoms + file accesses; all must be remembered to skip approval.
layers.example:
// governance/policy.go Evaluate()
1. rules    — first matching Rule wins (Allow/Deny/Ask)
2. safety   — read-only tools (read/ls/grep/...) → Allow
3. memory   — Recall; multi-key tools need ALL keys
4. human    — nil approver → Deny (fail closed)

layers.title: Two-tier memory + knowledge
layers.desc: Working memory: token-driven trim (70% of window or MaxWorkingTokens). Compressed: LLM incremental summary (8-section format), auto-triggered on overflow or via /compact. SessionStore messages are NEVER deleted. A separate MemoryProvider holds durable knowledge (preference/fact/lesson) with vector + keyword recall — self-evolution, not message archiving.

layers.title: ToolResult disk spill
layers.desc: DefaultResultPolicy: when a tool result's token count exceeds 5% of the model's context window, the content is written to /tmp/hwcloud/sess-<id>/artifact-<hex>.txt (long lines wrapped at 32K runes). The in-context result is replaced with a pointer; FileRef + Truncated flags set.

concept.title: Core concepts
concept.intro: The vocabulary of hwcloud — Agent is pure config; the runtime is the execution body; everything pluggable is an interface.

items.name: Agent
items.desc: Pure configuration: system prompts, model, guards, sub-agents, token budgets. No execution methods. Assembled into a Runtime via New(*agent.Agent, Deps).
items.example:
agent := agent.New(
    agent.WithModel(model),
    agent.WithSystemPrompts("You are..."),
    agent.WithSubAgents(...),
)
rt := kernel.New(agent, deps)

items.name: SubAgent
items.desc: A child agent registered as a plain tool (named after the agent, e.g. "researcher"). The parent delegates a sub-task via tool call; the child runs a full agent loop with isolated memory (no SessionStore), filtered tools, inherited guard, then returns its FinalOutput. Synchronous — the parent blocks until the child finishes. NOT transfer_to_*.

items.name: AGENTS.md / SOUL.md
items.desc: Static context profiles. AGENTS.md = working rules; SOUL.md = persona & limits. User-level (~/.hwcloud/profile/) + project-level ($(pwd)/) resolution; project overrides user.
items.example:
~/.hwcloud/profile/AGENTS.md   # user rules
./AGENTS.md                      # project rules (wins)

items.name: SubAgent (as-tool)
items.desc: Single-agent delegation: a parent agent registers a child as a plain tool and calls it for a sub-task. The child runs a full agent loop with isolated memory (no SessionStore), filtered tools, inherited guard, then returns its output. Synchronous — parent blocks until child finishes. Tool name is the agent name, NOT transfer_to_*.

items.name: Team (transfer_to_*)
items.desc: Control-transfer handoff: agents run one at a time in a sequential chain. When an agent calls transfer_to_X (EndTurn tool), control passes to agent X — the original agent's turn ends. Each agent has private memory (tool calls/results) + shared team memory. Loop detection: ping-pong (A-B-A-B) and frequency (≥3 visits). transfer_to_* is Team-exclusive — not SubAgent, not Orchestrate.

items.name: Orchestrate (DAG)
items.desc: Plan-and-execute: an LLM Planner decomposes the goal into a DAG once, before execution. The Executor runs steps in topological order with parallel batches (errgroup, max 8). Runtime is deterministic — no LLM except auto-replan on failure (rebuilds the affected subtree) and step summarization. Each step has an isolated session; upstream results shared as summaries.

items.name: Runtime
items.desc: The execution body. Runs the 7-stage loop, holds Deps-injected subsystems, manages tools/approver/memory per session. Created by kernel.New(agent, deps).

items.name: AgentContext
items.desc: Assembled every turn 0 by context.Runtime.Build(): system prompts + recalled knowledge + working memory + compressed summary. Updated per-turn with new messages.

items.name: Session
items.desc: Three modes: auto (tools execute immediately), manual (each non-readonly tool asks approval), plan (plan_create/plan_update before execution). Per-session state in SessionStore.
items.example:
./hwcloud serve --acp
# mode set via /mode or session/set_mode
# default_mode in settings.json

items.name: Policy
items.desc: The layered engine: rules → safety → memory → human. rules = first-match glob; safety = read-only auto-allow; memory = multi-key ALL; human = fail-closed.

items.name: ApprovalMemory
items.desc: Two implementations: SessionApprovalMemory (in-process) and PersistentApprovalMemory (store-backed, survives restarts). Remember/Recall keyed by tool + args; shell uses multi-key (atoms + files).

items.name: Decision
items.desc: The policy verdict: Allow, Deny (with reason), or Ask (route to human). Carries ModifiedArgs so a human can approve with edited arguments.

items.name: Working memory
items.desc: The recent message window, trimmed by token count. Budget = MaxWorkingTokens or 70% of the model's context window. Overflow trimmed from the bottom.

items.name: Compressed memory
items.desc: LLM-generated incremental summary in 8 sections (Claude Code format). Auto-triggered when working set overflows, or manually via /compact. Bounded by MaxCompressedTokens.

items.name: MemoryProvider
items.desc: A separate durable knowledge layer — NOT message archiving. Stores preference/fact/lesson entries with vector + keyword recall. LLM extractor turns finished runs into knowledge (self-evolution). Pluggable: SQLite (vector) or OpenViking (remote).

items.name: WASM Plugin
items.desc: 6 types: agent:tools, agent:observers (agent-side); cli:settings, cli:commands, cli:observers, cli:http (CLI-side). Any can declare cron-scheduled jobs. wazero runtime, Rust PDK, 28 host exports.

items.name: MCP
items.desc: Model Context Protocol client — imports external tools (browser, IaC, etc.) into the agent's tool set. Each tool call renders as a normal tool result.

items.name: Hook / Observer
items.desc: RunHooks: start/end callbacks sharing opaque state (OTEL spans nest, slog logs duration). Observer: enter/leave for each of the 7 stages — can abort the run.

items.name: IM channels
items.desc: Three platforms via one channel.Channel interface. Feishu: WebSocket + Schema 2.0 interactive cards (collapsible panels, tool-call cards, approval buttons, /mode), patch-based streaming. WeChat: ilinkai HTTP long-poll, plain-text one-shot replies (no card API), CDN media. WeCom: WebSocket + native streaming (message grows in place), template_card approvals. Process-level daemon; --channel flag or POST /connect starts it.
items.example:
./hwcloud serve --channel feishu
# QR scan → bot provisioned, creds saved
# process-level: frontend only triggers/observes
# /clear /mode (feishu) slash commands

items.name: Plan mode
items.desc: One of three session modes (auto/manual/plan). In plan mode, execution tools (shell/write/terminal) are removed; only read-only tools + plan_create/exit_plan_mode remain. The agent explores and decomposes, then exits to execute. plan_update (mark step status) works in ALL modes. enter_plan_mode/exit_plan_mode switch the tool set.
items.example:
// acp/server.go
enter_plan_mode → inject plan_create+exit
plan mode: shell/write removed, read-only kept
exit_plan_mode → restore previous mode

items.name: Process manager
items.desc: Background shell processes that persist across turns. Each gets a dir (stdout.log/stderr.log/exit.code); output writes to disk (not pipes) so it survives parent exit. The model reads /proc-<pid>/stdout.log and checks exit.code across turns. Per-session; cleanup kills all on session end.
items.example:
// process/manager.go
Create(cmd) → dir/<hex-id>/
SetPID(pid) → rename to proc-<pid>
model reads proc-<pid>/stdout.log

items.name: Sandbox
items.desc: OS-native confinement for shell/file/network. Linux: bubblewrap (bwrap) — new mount namespace, system paths read-only, workspace writable, --die-with-parent; PID namespace intentionally NOT unshared (so the model can kill processes). macOS: sandbox-exec + Seatbelt profile. Windows: NYI (runs unconfined with warning). Network isolation optional (--sandbox + network:isolated).
items.example:
./hwcloud serve --sandbox --port 8080
# bwrap: --ro-bind /usr, --bind /workspace
# --unshare-net (if network=isolated)
# bwrap missing → unconfined + warn

plugin.title: WASM Plugins
plugin.intro: Plugins are WASM modules (.wasm). Any language that compiles to WASM works — Rust, Go, TypeScript, Zig. The host (wazero) loads them in a sandboxed environment; a Rust SDK (hwcloud-pdk) wraps the FFI contract via the Plugin trait + export! macro. The ABI is simple enough to implement from any language.
plugin.cronNote: Any plugin type can also declare cron-scheduled jobs in its metadata — the host registers them with the scheduler and calls run_scheduled when they fire. See the cron detail section below.

types.name: agent:tools
types.desc: Adds custom tools to the agent — callable like shell/read/write. Tool name/description/parameters come from metadata().

types.name: agent:observers
types.desc: Hooks the agent's 7-stage run pipeline (enter/leave per stage). Returns continue or abort.

types.name: cli:settings
types.desc: Transforms settings.json at startup — merge env vars, add providers, inject config.

types.name: cli:commands
types.desc: Registers extra cobra subcommands into the CLI. One run_<name> export per leaf command.

types.name: cli:observers
types.desc: Monitors CLI command lifecycle — startup, shutdown, per-command enter/exit.

types.name: cli:http
types.desc: Registers custom HTTP routes served at /api/plugins/<name>/<path>. Input: HttpRequest, returns HttpResp.

plugin.abiDesc: Every plugin exports alloc/dealloc/metadata (required for host↔guest memory + type discovery). Each type adds its own entry-point export. Host↔guest communication uses packed (ptr,len) u64 — the high 32 bits are the WASM memory pointer, low 32 the length.
plugin.abiExports:
# Required for all types
alloc(size: u32) -> u32            # host→guest memory
dealloc(ptr: u32)                  # free input/output buffers
metadata() -> u64                  # packed PluginMeta JSON

# Per-type entry points (packed JSON in/out)
init(ptr, len) -> u64              # cli:settings
commands() -> u64                  # cli:commands
on_startup() / on_shutdown()       # cli:observers
on_command_start(ptr, len)         # cli:observers
on_command_end(ptr, len)           # cli:observers
execute(ptr, len) -> u64           # agent:tools
run(ptr, len) -> u64               # agent:observers
handle_request(ptr, len) -> u64    # cli:http
run_scheduled(ptr, len) -> u64     # scheduled jobs (any type)

examples.title: agent:tools — EchoPlugin
examples.desc: A tool the agent can call. plugin_type/name/description/parameters come from the trait; execute receives args JSON.

examples.title: agent:observers — LoggerPlugin
examples.desc: Hooks every stage. stage_filter ("*","*") means all stages, all phases; observe_stage returns continue or abort.

examples.title: scheduled job — EnvSyncPlugin
examples.desc: Declares a cron job in metadata; the host registers it and calls run_scheduled_job when it fires. Uses host::keyring_get + host::env_set.

plugin.hostDesc: Importable from any language. The host module exports exactly 28 functions; the Rust PDK declares the same 28 as FFI imports — the two sides agree.
plugin.cronDetailDesc: Vixie cron semantics: 5 fields (min hour dom month dow). When both dom and dow are restricted, they are ORed (13th OR Friday). 8-year search window so Feb 29 jobs survive non-leap years. Expressions that never match are rejected at registration. Second-resolution ticker, 30s job timeout, panic recovery, in-memory (re-registered from plugin metadata on restart).
plugin.cronDetailExample:
# 5-field Vixie cron
*/5 * * * *        every 5 minutes
0 9 * * 1-5       9am weekdays
0 0 13 * 5        13th OR Friday (OR logic)
0 0 29 2 *        Feb 29 (8-yr window finds next leap)
0 0 30 2 *        REJECTED — never matches

# scheduler.go
- ticker: 1 second
- job timeout: 30s
- no self-concurrency (running job skipped)
- missed runs dropped (no catch-up)
- panic recover (plugin crash ≠ host crash)
- in-memory: re-registered via Discover() on restart

iac.title: IAC MCP Server
iac.intro: A usage guide for IACMCPServer — deploy cloud infrastructure from AI chat via MCP.
iac.whatDesc: IACMCPServer is an MCP server that exposes cloud infrastructure deployment capabilities over the MCP protocol. Once configured in your agent, you can complete the full flow of "deploy a system to the cloud" in AI chat: requirement analysis → resource planning → cost estimation → deployment → troubleshooting → destruction.
iac.whatClient: Any MCP client (Claude Code, opencode, codearts, Cursor, hwcloud) can connect. For example, opencode's opencode.json:

paramRows.desc: Transport. local = stdio (local subprocess), remote = Streamable HTTP. IACMCPServer is a remote service — always use remote.
IACMCPServer access address — varies by connection method.
Whether this MCP service is enabled. Always true.
MCP connection handshake timeout (ms). Recommended for long-running tasks to avoid short default timeouts.
Under provider.models.<model> — declares the model supports function calling. Only needed for models via the opengw provider.

iac.urlInline: The value of url depends on where you connect from:
iac.urlDevSpace: Inside the dev space: IACMCPServer is already running and listening on port 9527 — url is http://localhost:9527.
iac.urlLocal: From your local machine: localhost in the dev space is unreachable; use a DevBridge tunnel to expose port 9527 as a public URL (e.g. https://<tunnel-id>-9527.cn-north-4-bridge.myhuaweicloud.com) and put that URL in the url field.
iac.urlSeeBelow: See "Connecting to IACMCPServer" below for detailed steps for both methods.
iac.capDesc: Tell it your need in natural language (e.g. "open a minimal ECS on Huawei Cloud with a public IP"), and it will:
features: Propose a plan — analyze the requirement, generate an architecture plan and deployment_id.
Specify resources — query real cloud APIs (flavors, images, availability zones), fill in concrete parameters.
Generate plan — write Terraform config, run terraform init + plan.
Estimate cost — query BSS pricing, return a monthly cost estimate.
Apply — run terraform apply, create real cloud resources.
Destroy — run terraform destroy, clean up all resources.
iac.caseDesc: Below is the full process of deploying an ECS via IACMCPServer in AI chat. You just issue instructions step by step in natural language; IACMCPServer calls cloud APIs, writes Terraform, and executes the deployment behind the scenes.

steps.title: Propose a plan
steps.prompt: Open a minimal ECS on Huawei Cloud cn-east-3, 40G system disk, with a public IP, OS OpenEuler.
steps.result:
✅ Plan generated, deployment_id: d-013
   - 1 × ECS (minimal spec)
   - 40G system disk
   - public EIP
   - OS: OpenEuler

steps.title: Specify resources
steps.result:
✅ Resources specified
   - Flavor: s7.small.1 (1C1G)
   - Image: OpenEuler 22.03
   - AZ: cn-east-3a

steps.title: Generate plan
steps.result:
✅ Plan generated
   - Will create 5 resources: VPC + subnet + security group + EIP + ECS
   - Planned changes: 5 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed

steps.title: Estimate cost
steps.result:
✅ Cost estimate complete
   - Estimated monthly: 92.74 CNY/month

steps.title: Apply
steps.result:
✅ Deployment complete
   - VPC: vpc-xxxx
   - Subnet: subnet-xxxx
   - Security group: sg-xxxx
   - EIP: 121.xxx.xxx.xxx
   - ECS: ecs-xxxx (s7.small.1, OpenEuler 22.03)

steps.title: Destroy
steps.result: ✅ Deployment d-013 destroyed, all resources deleted

iac.costWarnBody: apply is rejected if cost has not been estimated — this is a forced step to prevent unexpected charges.
iac.devSpaceTitle: Use directly inside the dev space
iac.devSpaceDesc: Inside the dev space (workspace), IACMCPServer is already running and listening on port 9527. Agents in the same environment need no tunnel or extra config — just point to the local port.
iac.devSpaceOpencode: Take opencode as an example — configure it in opencode.json. When opencode connects a model via the opengw provider, you must also declare tool_call: true in the provider section, or tool calls will not work:

fieldRows.effect: Declares the model supports function calling (tool calls).
fieldRows.miss: opencode does not send tool definitions to the model, or tool-call responses are not parsed — LLM output garbles.
Default timeout too short — connection may fail.

iac.toolCallNoteBody: tool_call is only needed for models connected via @ai-sdk/openai-compatible (the opengw provider). Built-in providers (e.g. codearts huaweicloud-maas) have tool-call support built in and do not need it. All models connected via opengw (deepseek, glm, etc.) should add it.
iac.devSpaceWarnBody: This method only works inside the dev space. To connect from an external device (your local machine, another host), expose the port via a DevBridge tunnel — see the tutorial below.
iac.bridgeTitle: Expose to external devices via DevBridge
iac.bridgeDesc: Use a Huawei Cloud DevBridge tunnel to securely expose IACMCPServer (port 9527) in the workspace as a public URL for remote AI tools to connect to.
iac.tunnelTitle: Create a tunnel in the workspace
iac.tunnelStep1: Start the DevBridge environment — open the dev space, find the devbridge environment, click Deploy → Start.
iac.tunnelStep2: Open the WebUI — after the environment starts, click WebUI to enter the DevBridge management console.
iac.tunnelStep3: Create a tunnel — in the WebUI, click Create Tunnel and fill in the name, description, and expiration time.
iac.anonWarnBody: Anonymous access lets anyone with the URL reach your IACMCPServer — mind your asset security. If IACMCPServer involves sensitive operations (e.g. cloud resource management), disable anonymous access.
iac.tunnelStep5: Host and get the URL — after configuration, click Host. The system generates a tunnel URL like:
iac.tunnelUrlDesc: This URL is the public access address of IACMCPServer.
iac.modifyNoteBody: To modify a port configuration (toggle anonymous access, change protocol, etc.), first Unhost, then modify, then re-Host — the new config takes effect only after re-hosting.
iac.aiConfigTitle: Configure the MCP connection in your AI tool
iac.methodAnonDesc: If the tunnel has anonymous access enabled, put the tunnel URL directly into your AI tool. Take opencode as an example — create or edit opencode.json in the project root:
iac.methodAnonNote: Replace <tunnel-id> with the actual tunnel ID generated after hosting. opencode can then remotely call the MCP tools provided by IACMCPServer via that URL.
iac.methodAuthDesc: If anonymous access is disabled, use the DevBridge CLI to establish an authenticated connection locally that maps the remote tunnel to a local port, then point your AI tool at the local port. Overall flow: install CLI → get AK/SK → login → connect tunnel to local port → configure AI tool to local port.
iac.aiInstallHintBody: Don't want to type commands manually? Copy the install command below and send it to your AI tool (e.g. opencode) — it will run the install for you.
iac.authStep1Desc: Run the following in a local terminal (works on Linux, macOS, and Windows):
iac.authStep1Path: After install, the CLI is at ~/.huawei/bin/devbridge. Add it to PATH.
iac.winNoteBody: Reopen the terminal after running the command for it to take effect.
iac.winCurlBody: Windows 10+ ships with curl. Run the install command in Git Bash or WSL. If bash is not found, install Git for Windows (which bundles bash) or enable WSL.
iac.authStep2Desc: The DevBridge CLI authenticates via Huawei Cloud IAM, requiring an AK (Access Key ID) and SK (Secret Access Key).
iac.authStep2Path1: 1. Open the Huawei Cloud console IAM page: https://console.huaweicloud.com/iam/
iac.authStep2Path2: 2. Hover over your profile (avatar/username) in the top-right corner, go to My Credentials → Access Keys tab.
iac.authStep2Path3: 3. Click Create Access Key. A credentials.csv file downloads containing the AK (e.g. AKxxxxxxxxxxxx) and SK (a long string).
iac.skWarnBody: The SK is displayed only at creation time — save it securely. If lost, you must recreate it. AK/SK are your cloud account credentials — never leak them or commit them to a code repository.
iac.authStep4Title: Step 4: connect the tunnel, map to a local port
iac.authStep4Desc: Use devbridge connect to connect the tunnel and map the remote service to a local port:
iac.authStep4Desc2: The <tunnel-id> is the ID generated when you created the tunnel in the WebUI (visible on the tunnel detail page). On success, the terminal shows:
iac.authStep4Out:
Connecting to tunnel: <tunnel-id>
Local port mapping: localhost:9527 → remote tunnel port 9527
Connection established
iac.authStep4Note: The remote IACMCPServer is now mapped to localhost:9527.
iac.connectNoteBody: devbridge connect is a foreground long-running command that occupies the terminal. Run it in a separate terminal window and keep it open. If it disconnects, re-run devbridge connect <tunnel-id> to resume.
iac.authStep5Title: Step 5: configure your AI tool to the local port
iac.authStep5Note: opencode now calls IACMCPServer via localhost:9527; traffic is forwarded through the authenticated DevBridge tunnel to the remote workspace.
iac.flowDiagram: opencode → localhost:9527 → devbridge connect (auth) → Huawei Cloud relay → workspace IACMCPServer:9527
notes: Tunnel expiration: default 8 hours, max 720 hours. The URL becomes invalid after expiry — re-host to continue.
Anonymous access risk: once enabled, anyone with the URL can reach your IACMCPServer. Ensure IACMCPServer has proper auth, or only share the URL within a trusted scope.
Config changes: modify port config → Unhost → modify → re-Host.
Tunnel cleanup: unhost and delete the tunnel when done to avoid residual resources.
Dev use only: DevBridge is a dev tunneling service, not for production.
CLI connection: devbridge connect must keep running in the terminal; closing the terminal breaks the connection. Re-run devbridge connect <tunnel-id> to resume.
AK/SK security: the SK is shown only once — keep it safe. Never write AK/SK into a code repository or share them.
